response.why: batch: player A starts
2 Mountains with T1 Lightning Bolt and T2 Dragon Fodder is a solid aggro start. 3x Dragon Fodder + removal gives good reach and board presence. Keep.
Turn 1 main phase: always play a land first. Mountain into Lightning Bolt sets up aggressive early pressure.

Turn 1, empty board on both sides. No creatures to remove yet, and burning face on T1 without board pressure doesn't accelerate my clock. Hold Lightning Bolt for creature removal or reach after they develop. Pass.
Begin Combat with no creatures. No reason to act—I'll declare no attackers and move to their turn. Hold Lightning Bolt.
No creatures to attack with on turn 1. Pass to End Combat, then end turn.
End Combat—pass to postcombat main phase.
Postcombat main with 1 Mountain—can't cast Dragon Fodder (costs {1}{R}, need 2 mana). No reason to act. Pass to end my turn.
End Turn—pass to opponent's turn. Hold Lightning Bolt ready for creature removal or emergency removal if they develop flyers.
Opponent's turn, Upkeep. Nothing to interact with yet. Yield until my turn, but engine will wake me if they play a creature.

Spyglass Siren is flying—my ground creatures can't block it. It will deal recurring unavoidable damage if left alive. Kill it now with Lightning Bolt before it becomes a clock I can't answer. Save Incinerate and Dragon Fodders for later board pressure.
Target Spyglass Siren. Lightning Bolt deals 3 damage to its 1 toughness, killing it and preventing recurring flying damage I can't block.
Upkeep with nothing to do. Pass to Draw step and move into my main phase to play lands and cast Dragon Fodder.
Draw phase—pass to Precombat Main. I'll play Mountain and cast Dragon Fodder to build board presence.
Play my second Mountain. Always play a land before casting spells. This gives me {R}{R} for Dragon Fodder next.
Cast Dragon Fodder. Creates 2 goblin tokens that will attack next turn. With {R}{R} from 2 Mountains, I can afford {1}{R}. Board presence matters more than holding removal right now.
Upkeep—nothing to interact with. Pass to Draw, then reassess. Opponent is building mana (2 Darkslick Shores) but no creatures visible yet besides Map Token.

Draw phase—pass to Precombat Main. I have Dragon Fodder x2, Incinerate x2, Lightning Bolt in hand. Opponent has built mana but no creatures yet—unusual. Plan to attack with my goblin and assess threats.

Cast Dragon Fodder. Opponent is durdle-ing (no creatures), so I accelerate my board. Creates 2 more goblins (3 total). I'll attack this turn for 3 damage + burn for reach to close out the game. Don't waste time—every turn they're doing nothing, I'm hitting face.

Leaf 0 (no attack): solid board but no progress. Leaf 1 (attack): deal 1 damage + race. Opponent is durdle-ing with no creatures, so every damage matters. Tapped goblin is fine—they have no way to attack. Attack to advance the win condition.

Kill Deep-Cavern Bat with Lightning Bolt. It's flying (can't block with goblins) and has lifelink (damages my race). The instructions say 'Burn the Bat'—do it before it attacks and closes the game via life drain. Use Lightning Bolt (cheaper than Incinerate) and keep racing.

Target Deep-Cavern Bat. Lightning Bolt deals 3 damage, killing it. Removes the flying threat that can't be blocked and has lifelink. Bat exiled a card from my hand, but killing it returns that card (exile ends when bat leaves).
Lightning Bolt resolved. Pass through Upkeep to Draw step. Continue the game (bat should be dead from the 3 damage).
Deep-Cavern Bat is dead. Upkeep—pass to Draw step and continue attacking.
Draw—pass to Precombat Main. Shock is good reach, but I'll hold it to see what they play next turn. If they still durdle, I'll burn face after attacking. 3 goblins + burn should close the race soon.
Precombat Main—pass to combat. I want to attack with my 3 goblins first, then burn in postcombat main after they've committed (or chosen not to block). This maximizes the damage sequence.
Begin Combat—pass to Declare Attackers. I'll attack with all 3 goblins.

Leaf 0 (no attack): wasting time when ahead. Leaf 1 (attack-all): maximize damage output, 3 goblins × turns + burn = lethal. Leaves 2-4 (hold 1 goblin): unnecessary—opponent has no creatures to block against, and holding back delays the kill. Attack all 3.
All 3 goblins declared as attackers, now tapped. Pass to resolve combat damage (3 damage to opponent, going to 16 life). Move to postcombat main where I'll burn.
Declare Blockers—opponent has no creatures to block with. Pass to combat damage phase where my 3 goblins deal 3 damage, bringing opponent to 16 life.
Combat Damage resolves: 3 damage dealt, opponent at 16 life. Pass to End Combat, then postcombat main where I'll burn them out.
End Combat—pass to postcombat main. Burn them for lethal: Shock (2) + Incinerate x2 (6) = 8 damage. Opponent at 16, this finishes them.
Cast Shock for 2 damage (opponent to 14 life). Burn face to tighten the race. Next turn: attack + remaining Incinerates for lethal. Current mana is limited, so burn now and win next turn.
Target opponent face with Shock for 2 damage (16 → 14 life). Closing out next turn with burn + goblins.
Cast Incinerate on opponent face (14 → 11 life). Racing to lethal: burn now + goblins in combat + second Incinerate in Precombat Main seals the win.
Incinerate to opponent face (14 → 11 life). Continuing lethal burn plan: Draw step, Precombat Main cast second Incinerate (11 → 8), then Combat phase goblins close it out.

All attacks lead to winning position. Attack-all (leaf 1) maximizes damage pressure: 3 goblins hit for 3, postcombat Incinerates finish for 6 more (11 → 2 life), setting up turn 10 win. Holding goblins (leaves 2-4) suboptimal—no reason to preserve creatures. Not attacking (leaf 0) wastes momentum and gives opponent chance to stabilize with Kaito.

Cast Incinerate to kill Enduring Curiosity (4/3). Although it returns as an enchantment, destroying the creature now prevents 4 damage per attack and slows opponent's card draw engine. Still on track: 11 - 3 (Incinerate) - 3 (goblins next combat) - 3 (final Incinerate) = 2 life, close to lethal next turn.

Target Enduring Curiosity (4/3). Kill the creature now to prevent its card-draw ability from triggering on my goblin attacks. It returns as an enchantment but loses evasion. Opponent drops to 11 life, then goblins + final burn next turn closes the game.

All attacks lead to winning endgame. Attack-all (leaf 1) maximizes pressure: 3 goblins hit for 3, postcombat burn (Incinerate + Searing Spear) for 6 = 9 total damage (11 → 2 life). Holding goblins (leaves 2-4) wastes tempo. Not attacking (leaf 0) unnecessarily extends the game—finish aggressively.

Cast Incinerate for 3 damage (11 → 8 life). Opponent developed Floodpits Drowner and Preacher of the Schism, both summoning sick. Burn down before they become threats. Next turn: attack goblins + Searing Spear finishes (8 - 3 - 3 = 2, close to lethal on turn 14).

Burn opponent face (11 → 8 life). Both Floodpits Drowner and Preacher of the Schism are summoning sick and can't attack yet. Race to lethal is better than removing creatures. Next turn: Searing Spear (8 → 5) + goblin attacks (5 → 2) = nearly there.

Attack-all (leaves 2-3) optimal: even blocked, deal 1 damage uncontested, then Searing Spear in postcombat (3 more) = 4 total, opponent to 4 life. Leaf 1 worst-case (both block, 0 damage) still recoverable. Hold patterns (leaves 4-9) preserve creatures but commit less damage this turn when opponent is at 8 life—unnecessary caution. Race to lethal: attack-all + burn finishes next turn.

Opponent blocking (leaves 1-2) preferable to no-blocks (leaf 0) where I take 4 damage. Leaf 1 (Floodpits blocks) is best: fair trade (my goblin for opponent's 2/1), limits opponent damage to 2. Leaf 2 (Preacher blocks) worse: lose goblin for free against 2/4 blocker, still take 2 damage. Leaf 0 (no blocks) worst: goblin connects unblocked but opponent deals 4 total damage with Floodpits + ? (now at 11 life).

Cast Searing Spear for 3 damage (8 → 5 life). Opponent close to dead. Goblin still on board for next turn attack. Even if opponent stabilizes temporarily, lethal is 1-2 turns away with burn + goblins.

Burn opponent face (8 → 5 life). Searing Spear to the dome closes the race. Opponent's creatures mostly summoning sick or tapped. Next turn: attack with goblin, cast remaining burn or threats to finish.

Both leaves show opp_life 0 (lethal reached), but attack-all (leaf 1) is the correct aggressive finish: Goblin hits for 1 damage (5 → 4), postcombat burn/threats close it out next turn. Attack-none (leaf 0) is passive and unnecessarily extends the game. When ahead, attack and finish—don't stall.

Tap Mountain for mana. Cast Monastery Swiftspear (haste, 1/2) for {R} to attack this turn for 1 damage (6 → 5 life). I'm at 4 life vs opponent at 6—need to race. Swiftspear + future Dragon Fodder tokens close the game next turn.

Tap Mountain for {R} to have {R}{R} total. Cast Monastery Swiftspear ({R}) with haste to attack this turn for 1 damage (6 → 5). Then cast Dragon Fodder ({1}{R}) to create 2 tokens for next turn's attack. Racing hard at 4 life vs 6.
